title: OmniFlow retail POC kickoff and success metrics
content:
Purpose and high level goal:
This kickoff captures scope and measurable success criteria for the OmniFlow retail POC. Customer goal: reduce time-to-recommend and increase click-through for cross-channel product suggestions by proving a production-ready inference and retrieval pipeline that can run on Dedicated or Private deployment with predictable latency and cost bounds.

POC hypothesis:
If we serve a hybrid retrieval-augmented recommendations pipeline (embedding store + lightweight reranker) using Redwood Dedicated with KV-cache and prefix caching enabled, then OmniFlow will see:
- 20% lift in organic CTR on suggested SKU modules during pilot queries
- median inference latency <= 180ms for 1–2k-context retrieval + rank
- 99% successful request rate under a 50 req/s sustained load profile
- operational cost estimate under $0.50 per thousand inference-equivalent requests (pilot config)

Scope (what's in):
- Integrate customer product catalog snapshots (S3 export) and 90k product vectors into Redis/FAISS store compatible with Redwood cache layer.
- Implement lightweight reranker model (distil-bert sized) served behind Redwood API and a fallback open model.
- End-to-end demo: search -> retrieve -> rerank -> recommend card in web storefront staging.
- Load test at 50 req/s and spike to 200 req/s for short burst.
- Basic observability: per-route latency, token-level cost, failure traces, and sample output logs.

Out of scope (for POC):
- Full A/B across production cohorts, personalization beyond catalog history, multi-region failover (only single region).

Success criteria (pass/fail and metrics):
- Functional: demo flow returns plausible recommendations for 90% of validation queries (validation set of 500 real queries).
- Quality: Recall@10 >= 0.6 on curated evaluation set; NDCG@5 improvement >= 12% vs baseline fuzzy-match.
- Latency: median end-to-end <= 180ms; p95 <= 350ms under steady 50 req/s.
- Reliability: 99% success rate for requests across 60-minute load test.
- Cost: pilot cost estimate documented and below threshold. If all 5 categories meet thresholds -> POC considered successful.

Data and privacy notes:
- Customer will provide S3 manifest and 1 snapshot of catalog CSV (no PII expected).
- For Private deploy variant, data-at-rest must use customer KMS; document required key IDs by workshop day 2.

Workshop agenda (Day 0 - Day 3):
Day 0: Pre-kickoff prep (data schema, IAM access, Slack channel, Confluence page).
Day 1 (Onsite/workshop): architecture walkthrough, integration checklist, initial data ingest run, vectorization config decisions, fallback policy discussion.
Day 2: Model/re-ranker selection, quantization tradeoffs, runtime config (batch sizes, KV cache TTL), security & KMS plan.
Day 3: Load test, observability dashboard review, success criteria review, handoff & next steps.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Customer product lead: Emily Torres (provide dataset, capture business metrics).
- Solutions engineering (owner): Riley Johnson (integration, config, deliverables).
- Applied ML: Asha Patel (eval, retrieval/rerank configs).
- SRE/infra: Marco Nguyen (load testing, capacity planning).
- Sales/CS: Priya Desai (commercial terms, procurement).

Risks and mitigations:
- Catalog contains noisy SKUs -> mitigation: add preprocessing step and small manual curation sample.
- Latency exceeds targets under realistic query patterns -> mitigation: enable prefix/KV cache, tune batching, test quantized model variant.
- Access delays to customer S3 -> mitigation: mirror a small sample to Redwood staging for iterative work.

Open questions (to resolve in workshop):
- Does customer require on-prem model weights storage or is VPC Private enough?
- Expected realistic burst patterns during seasonal promotions? Provide traces if available.
- Approval timeline for KMS/HSM onboarding.

Deliverables and timeline (4 week cadence):
Week 0: Kickoff workshop + raw ingest into staging.
Week 1: Retrieval + embedding quality loop, reranker prototype.
Week 2: Integration with Redwood routes, caching and batch tuning, initial load testing.
Week 3: Final validation, cost estimate, runbook, handoff doc, executive summary + demo.

Validation artifacts to hand over:
- Sample request/response logs (anonymized).
- Evaluation notebook with Recall/NDCG tables and prompts used.
- Load test report (k6/locust) and observability screenshots.
- Runbook: how to change model, rollback, scale capacity.

Immediate next steps (within 48 hours):
1) Customer to grant S3 read role and share small schema sample (Emily).
2) Riley to provision Redwood staging project and invite core collaborators.
3) Asha to draft evaluation template and baseline metrics import.
4) Marco to schedule load test window and prepare capacity matrix.

Notes to self / working items:
- Try 8-bit quantized reranker if p95 > 400ms.
- Keep fallback chain: distil reranker -> open LLM lightweight -> cached top-N.
- Check with legal on sample data sharing checklist before ingest.

Appendix: quick checklist for kickoff meeting:
- Confirm Slack channel and Confluence links present.
- IAM access validated for Redwood staging.
- Sample 500 queries uploaded to shared folder.
- KMS requirements documented if Private option chosen.

Document history: created by Riley Johnson, initial draft 2024-11-14. Revised through engineering review 2025-01-25.
